- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.1) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment runs — model fails to recognize downward momentum.
- When sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection lag.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show strong upward trend, cap forecast peak at 1–2 std dev above recent mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights early sentiment signals — adjust by dampening initial forecast spikes if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid “sentiment blindness”.
- Forecast should not exceed 2x recent 10-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.3) and confirmed over 3 days.
